{{Reg polyhedra db|Reg star polyhedron stat table|gI}}
[[File:Great icosahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of a great icosahedron]]

In [[geometry]], the '''great icosahedron''' is one of four [[Kepler–Poinsot polyhedra]] ([[nonconvex]] [[List of regular polytopes#Non-convex 2|regular polyhedra]]), with [[Schläfli symbol]] {{math|{3,{{frac|5|2}}} }} and [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]] of {{CDD|node_1|3|node|5|rat|d2|node}}. It is composed of 20 intersecting triangular faces, having five triangles meeting at each vertex in a [[pentagram]]mic sequence.

The great icosahedron can be constructed analogously to the pentagram, its two-dimensional analogue, via the extension of the {{math|(''n''–1)}}-dimensional [[simplex]] faces of the core {{mvar|n}}-polytope (equilateral triangles for the great icosahedron, and [[line segment]]s for the pentagram) until the figure regains regular faces. The [[grand 600-cell]] can be seen as its four-dimensional analogue using the same process.

==Construction ==
The edge length of a great icosahedron is <math>\frac{7+3\sqrt{5}}{2} = \left(\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}2\right)^4</math> times that of the original icosahedron.

== Formulas ==

For a great icosahedron with edge length {{mvar|E}} (the edge of its dodecahedron core),

{| style="height: 300px" align=center
| align="right" | [[Inradius]]: || <math>\quad E \times \frac{3\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{15}}{4}</math>
|-
| align="right" | [[Midradius]]: || <math>\quad E \times \frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4}</math>
|-
| align="right" | [[Circumradius]]: || <math>\quad E \times \frac{\sqrt{2(5-\sqrt{5})}}{4}</math>
|-
| align="right" | [[Surface area]]: || <math>\quad E^2 \times 3\sqrt{3}\Bigl(5+4\sqrt{5}\Bigr)</math>
|-
| align="right" | [[Volume]]: || <math>\quad E^3 \times \frac{25+9\sqrt{5}}{4}</math>
|}

== As a snub ==
The ''great icosahedron'' can be constructed as a uniform [[Snub (geometry)|snub]], with different colored faces and only [[tetrahedral symmetry]]: {{CDD|node_h|3x|rat|d2|node_h|3x|rat|d2|node_h}}. This construction can be called a ''retrosnub tetrahedron'' or ''retrosnub tetratetrahedron'',<ref>{{KlitzingPolytopes|../incmats/gike.htm|uniform polyhedra|Great icosahedron}}</ref> similar to the [[snub tetrahedron]] symmetry of the [[icosahedron]], as a partial faceting of the [[truncated octahedron]] (or ''[[omnitruncation|omnitruncated]] tetrahedron''): {{CDD|node_h|3|node_h|3|node_h}}. It can also be constructed with 2 colors of triangles and [[pyritohedral symmetry]] as, {{CDD|node_h|3x|rat|d2|node_h|4|node}} or {{CDD|node_h|3x|rat|d2|node_h|4|rat|3x|node}}, and is called a ''retrosnub octahedron''.

== Related polyhedra ==
[[File:Great stellated dodecahedron truncations.gif|thumb|Animated truncation sequence from {{math|{5/2, 3} }} to {{math|{3, 5/2} }}]]
It shares the same [[vertex arrangement]] as the regular convex [[icosahedron]]. It also shares the same [[edge arrangement]] as the [[small stellated dodecahedron]].

A truncation operation, repeatedly applied to the great icosahedron, produces a sequence of uniform polyhedra. Truncating edges down to points produces the [[great icosidodecahedron]] as a rectified great icosahedron. The process completes as a birectification, reducing the original faces down to points, and producing the [[great stellated dodecahedron]].

The [[Truncation (geometry)|truncated]] ''great stellated dodecahedron'' is a degenerate polyhedron, with 20 triangular faces from the truncated vertices, and 12 (hidden) doubled up pentagonal faces ({{math|{{mset|10/2}}}}) as truncations of the original pentagram faces, the latter forming two [[great dodecahedron|great dodecahedra]] inscribed within and sharing the edges of the icosahedron.
